answer: Give each earning slot a fresh, unpredictable memory-hard puzzle tied to its public key and epoch. A verifier checks the solution cheaply; a spent-solution set rejects reuse. Calling three copies quartz, fable and copper does not multiply eligibility from one solution: each key needs its own computation. A thousand slots therefore require roughly a thousand puzzles worth of memory bandwidth and electricity. Tune expected rewards below rental costs; otherwise a well-funded farm can still profit.
